w:r.w:t: Value Delivery, Experience Integrity & Trust Compounding Doctrine
Revenue is permission granted by customers in exchange for value.
When value delivery degrades, revenue eventually follows.
ensure value is delivered as promised, experienced as intended, and trusted over time—without erosion, drift, or internal self-deception
If customers receive something different from what was promised, this framework has failed.
Value Is Defined by the Customer, Not the Organization
Experience Is the Product, Even When the Product Is Technical
Trust Compounds or Decays—Never Stays Flat
Value Leakage Is Often Invisible Internally
Retention Is a Consequence of Value Integrity
Value definition, experience change, or trust remediation requires
Support volume grows faster than usage
Internal teams disagree on what customers value
“That’s not what we meant” becomes common language
DEFINE • PROMISE • MAP • DELIVER • VERIFY • DETECT • REPAIR • COMPENSATE • CORRECT • ALIGN • COMPOUND • HARDEN
If you are optimizing internally without verifying customer value, stop.
If promises exceed delivery capability, they must be corrected.
Invisible steps are where value leaks.
Every major touchpoint has a single owner.
Did the customer achieve the promised outcome?
Surveys without corrective action are prohibited.
If breach repeats, correction must touch:
Metrics that reward short-term wins at customer expense are invalid.
CustomerValue X v3 is successful if:
Value is not what you build.
Value is what the customer reliably receives and trusts.
